Licences & Attribution

Last updated: 15 October 2026 [TO CONFIRM: effective date]

Yestermanac is built on open knowledge. This page credits each source and states its licence. The open licences below are not changed by our Terms of Use; you keep every right they give you.

Wikipedia text — CC BY-SA 4.0

  • Event, birth, death and holiday texts come from Wikipedia's date pages, written by Wikipedia contributors.
  • They are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International licence (CC BY-SA 4.0).
  • Credit line: “Text from Wikipedia contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0.” Each entry links to its source page, and the app records the revision it was taken from.
  • We remove wiki markup. Texts machine-translated from another language are marked as such.

ShareAlike

If you adapt Wikipedia-derived text, including text you copy from the app, you must share your adaptation under CC BY-SA 4.0 (or a compatible licence), give credit, link to the licence and indicate changes. We treat our own summaries and translations of Wikipedia text the same way: they are released under CC BY-SA 4.0 too. We do not add any restriction to this text.

Wikidata — CC0

Structured data (links between entries, countries, coordinates and labels in many languages) comes from Wikidata and is released under CC0 1.0. CC0 needs no credit; we credit Wikidata anyway. Region names used for holidays also come from Wikidata.

Wikimedia Commons pictures — licence per file

  • Pictures come from Wikimedia Commons. Every file has its own licence chosen by its author, for example a Creative Commons licence or the public domain.
  • The app shows a picture only when it has both an author and a licence, and prints them with the picture. Tapping the credit opens the file's Commons page, which states the full terms.
  • The licence on each file's Commons page is the one that applies to it.

Public holidays — python-holidays (MIT)

Public and regional holiday dates are generated with python-holidays, released under the MIT licence. [TO CONFIRM: version used for the release data and the exact copyright line from its LICENSE file]. Dates that follow a lunar calendar are marked “estimated”.

Languages and countries — Unicode CLDR

The list of countries where each language is official, and the grouping of countries into world regions, are derived from the Unicode Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR), release 46, Copyright © Unicode, Inc. CLDR data is used under the Unicode License. [TO CONFIRM: licence version and notice text from the CLDR 46 release].

Time zones — IANA tz database

City coordinates for the almanac's default place come from the IANA time zone database, which is in the public domain.

Fonts

The app does not bundle any font files. It uses the fonts installed on your device, which are licensed to you by your device or operating-system maker (on Android usually Roboto under the Apache License 2.0 and Noto under the SIL Open Font License 1.1). [TO CONFIRM: no bundled fonts in the release build]. This website uses only your device's system fonts and loads no web fonts.

Software libraries

The app includes open-source libraries, among them Android Jetpack (AndroidX, Compose, WorkManager, Glance), Kotlin and kotlinx, Coil, OkHttp and the Solana Mobile Wallet Adapter, released under the Apache License 2.0. [TO CONFIRM: full list and notices from the release build's dependency report].
